findings.evidence: tests/managed_task_exact_state_cases.py loads managed_task.py as "managed_task_exact_state", tests/managed_start_transaction_cases.py loads start_managed_task.py as "managed_start_transaction_cases_impl", and tests/test_worktree_hygiene.py uses f"{name}_under_test". Each of these is a separate instance of a file that other tests load under its canonical name. tests/_platform_modules.py identity_violations() says 'A private instance under a name nothing registers is self-contained' and does not flag them. The spec's guard clause covers only a differing instance 'of the same name', so this is consistent with the guard text but not with the broader 'share one module instance' sentence.
findings.summary: The platform-ci requirement says code under test and every test in a process share one module instance. Several tests still load the same source file under a private alias name, which creates a second instance of that file. The guard allows this by design, so the 'one instance' wording is stricter than what is enforced.
